BUSINESS PLAN - KGALAGADI BOREHOLE VEGETABLES (PTY) LTD

1. Executive summary
Kgalagadi Borehole Vegetables will grow, pack and deliver fresh vegetables to supermarkets and school feeding programmes in Gaborone and Kanye. We request P 650,000 from CEDA. The owners contribute P 150,000 in cash and P 100,000 in equipment.

2. Management team
Mpho Kgosi (Managing Director) has 11 years of experience in horticulture, including 6 years as farm manager at a commercial farm. Curriculum vitae and certificates are attached. Keletso Dube (Operations) holds a diploma in agricultural engineering.

3. Market
Target market: 14 supermarkets, 9 schools and 40 restaurants within 120 km. Market size is estimated at 85 tonnes of vegetables a month, based on our own survey of 23 buyers (Annex C). Demand is strong in winter when local supply drops.
Competitors: three commercial growers and imported produce from South Africa. Our market share target is 8% in year 1 rising to 15% by year 4. Selling price is P 9.50 per kg against a competitor average of P 10.20 per kg. Cost price is P 6.10 per kg, so profit per kg is P 3.40.
We hold three letters of intent from Choppies, two schools and one restaurant group.

4. Marketing and distribution
We will promote through direct sales visits and a WhatsApp ordering line. Deliveries are made twice weekly with our own refrigerated truck.

5. Operations
Production process: seedlings, drip irrigation from the borehole, harvesting, grading, packing. Maximum capacity is 120 tonnes per month on 4 hectares. Plant life of drip equipment is 10 years.
Land: Tribal land allocation (Land Board certificate attached), plot 4412 Kanye. Borehole drilled 2019, completion certificate and water test attached. Soil test attached.
Suppliers: three seed suppliers and two fertiliser suppliers; if one fails, we switch to the next. Three quotations were obtained for the irrigation system and truck (Annex D).

6. Implementation schedule
Month 1 order equipment; month 2 install drip system; month 3 plant first crop; month 5 first harvest and sales.

7. Staff
Eight employees: a supervisor, 6 farm workers and a driver. Wages total P 14,500 per month. Staff will be trained in food safety by the Ministry of Agriculture.

8. Financial projections
Projected annual revenue: P 2,150,000 in year 1
Projected annual operating expenses: P 1,590,000
Cash flow projection for five years is in Annex E, including loan repayments, tax and asset purchases. Balance sheet and income statement for 5 years are attached. Assumptions: depreciation 10%, tax rate 22%, sales volume 70 tonnes per month in year 1.

9. Risks
Cost overruns on the irrigation system are covered by a 10% contingency. Slower sales: we have signed letters of intent for 40% of output. Technical risk: borehole failure; we hold a spare pump. Environmental impact: drip irrigation limits water use.
Sensitivity analysis: if sales fall by 20%, profit falls to P 180,000 but loan instalments are still covered. The truck and equipment are insured. If the owner is ill, the supervisor takes over.

10. SWOT
Strengths: experienced owner, own water. Weaknesses: single borehole. Opportunities: school feeding demand. Threats: imports, drought.

11. Licences
We hold a trading licence (BW2019-4412) and tax clearance certificate. The company is registered with CIPA.

12. Benefits
The project creates 8 jobs in Kanye and buys inputs from local suppliers, benefiting the community and the economy.

13. Security
The truck (cost P 320,000, market value P 280,000, forced-sale value P 210,000) is offered as security.
